text:
maya: Heads up — after the v2-checkpoint onboarding this morning we're seeing p99 latency oscillations on the staging shard. Not steady spike, more like bursts every ~30s.

ci-bot: perf-ci: nightly-staging-check FAILED for commit 9f3a2b7 (tokenizer/config bump). p95 +18%, p99 +45%. See CI dashboard: https://ci.redwood/pipeline/1122/results

maya: Attachments from profiling: kernel selection shows frequent fallback from optimized_fwd_q8 -> generic_fwd for some requests. Also KV-prefetch queue depth spikes.

tj: Do we have a sample request that triggers it?

maya: Short thread of logs from one noisy worker: 
```
[2026-03-17 09:12:04] request_id=abc123 model=v2-checkpoint seq_len=512 kernel=optimized_fwd_q8 -> select_failed reason=tokenizer_length_mismatch
[2026-03-17 09:12:04] kvcache: prefetch enqueue latency=240ms queue_depth=78
[2026-03-17 09:12:05] kernel_switch: fallback to generic_fwd path latency_penalty=35ms
[2026-03-17 09:12:34] batch_flush reason=idle strat=heuristic-v2 batch_size=1
```

maya: The tokenizer length distribution changed: more long-prefix cases after the tokenizer's new normalization. That is shifting kernel heuristics and causing prefetch backpressure.

alec: Hmm. Could be two interactions: tokenizer increases average prefix length -> KV prefetch issues -> batcher sees fewer good coalescing opportunities -> falls back to conservative kernel which triggers more CPU fallback.

anna: Any regressions in the kernel selector unit tests?

maya: Unit tests pass. This only shows at scale with real request mix. Repro is possible in a small perf harness by replaying a sampled 10k requests with the new tokenizer; I ran that and reproduced the oscillation pattern.

tj: What's the immediate mitigation? Revert checkpoint? Patch tokenizer? Kernel selector tweak?

maya: Short-term I'd like to throttle prefetch depth and force prefer_optimized for v2 unless prefetch queue depth > 200ms. That avoids the fallback cascade. Longer term we need to update kernel heuristics to account for new tokenization length distribution.

ci-bot: revert-candidate: commit 9f3a2b7 flagged by perf-guard. Approve revert? (ops tag)

alec: Before revert, can we try a hotfix in staging: change config: `kvcache.prefetch.max_inflight = 16` and `kernel_selector.prefer_optimized = true` for model:v2-checkpoint.

maya: Pushed a canary: `kubectl apply -f staging/overrides/v2-prefetch-throttle.yaml` — it flips the two settings for the model route. Monitoring now.

anna: Any dashboards to watch?

maya: Watch /dashboards/eng-runtime/p99-latency and /dashboards/kvcache/prefetch-latency. Also kernel-selector metric `kernel_fallback_rate{model="v2-checkpoint"}`.

(2m later)

maya: Canary looks promising. p95 back down near baseline, p99 spikes reduced. Example: before fix p99=420ms, after canary p99=280ms. Still slightly above baseline but far better.

tj: Good. We should still bisect the runtime changes in the last two merges. Which commits touched kernel selector heuristics?

alec: Candidate list: 1) 8b4f6cc kernel-selector refactor (3 days ago), 2) a1d2c3f batcher heuristics tweak (5 days ago), 3) 9f3a2b7 tokenizer/config bump (onboard). The CI flagged 9f3a2b7 but the selector refactor could have changed sensitivity.

maya: I ran a quick bisect harness pairing combinations. Results: with old kernel-selector + new tokenizer = small degradation (~+10% p99). With new kernel-selector + old tokenizer = small improvement. With new kernel-selector + new tokenizer = worst (+45%). So interaction effect.

anna: That points to heuristic sensitivity. Options: revert tokenizer; revert kernel refactor; or tune selector to be conservative for models with changed length distribution.

tj: For production rollback policy, prefer non-revert if we can patch fast. Patch kernel selector to consider tokenization stats when picking kernels. Quick patch idea: add `expected_prefix_len` signal from model metadata and bias kernel_score by 0.2 when mismatch.

maya: I prototyped `kernel_score += 0.25 if abs(prefix_len - expected) < threshold` — in harness it reduced fallback by 60%. I'll open PR with tests + perf harness reproducer.

alec: Also add telemetry tag so when selector picks generic_fwd we emit `selector_reason=tokenizer_len_mismatch`. That will make future debugging easier.

ci-bot: PR created: #4187 maya "selector: consider tokenizer prefix stat for kernel scoring" — perf-run scheduled.

maya: Plan: 1) keep canary throttle in staging for 24h, 2) land selector patch behind feature flag + enable for v2 route in staging, 3) run 24h perf replay + CI, 4) if stable, roll to production. If perf still bad -> revert checkpoint.

anna: Sounds good. Please add rollback steps to the PR description (revert override + revert PR).

maya: Will do. Also creating a short note for the release docs: "Onboarding checklist: run tokenizer length-distribution check and update model-metadata.expected_prefix_len".

tj: Thanks. Keep us posted — ping @ops if p99 crosses 500ms. :thumbsup:

maya: pinging once more when patch results land.

(automated) ci-bot: perf-run #4187 finished: p95 delta -2%, p99 delta +4% (on staging harness). Need longer run to be sure.

maya: Ok leaving canary for 6h then we'll decide.

alec: If anyone wants to reproduce locally I left a small harness script: `scripts/replay_sample.sh --model v2-checkpoint --sample 10000 --tokenizer v2`. It injects token lengths based on sampled distribution.

maya: Thanks team. We'll follow up in another thread with final decision.
